conventions.convention: Deletion retains the original sample size n and retained indices as inputs. Stability is uniform over every sample, deleted index and test observation; deletion coefficient β_n implies replacement coefficient 2β_n.
RKHS deletion objectives retain denominator m and regularizer λ times the squared norm. Minima are assumed attained; λ>0, σ≥0 and κ≥0. Stability alone supplies no bounded-loss constant.
Expected generalization uses a finite IID product sample, jointly measurable full/deleted test losses, measurable risk maps and a common finite loss bound. Its conclusions are choice-free.
The empirical-risk and leave-one-out confidence bounds each have probability at least 1−δ separately; simultaneous validity is not asserted. AC is assumed through McDiarmid.
Rademacher complexity uses the one-sided sign supremum without absolute values and normalization 1/m.
The nearest-neighbor rule votes among all observations at minimum distance, resolves tied votes by 0, and predicts 1 on the empty sample. The instability witness is asserted for m≥2.

load_bearing.statement: Uniform deletion stability requires |L(A_S,z)−L(A_{S\setminus i},z)|≤β_n for every n≥1, S∈Z^n, i∈[n], and z∈Z, using the size-indexed deletion output.

Under its stated measurable supervised setting, IID product sample, deterministic permutation-invariant size-indexed rule, bounded full/deleted losses and finite nonincreasing deletion-stability sequence: E[R_P(A_S)−R̂_S(A_S)]≤2β_m, E[R_P(A_S)−R_loo(A,S)]≤β_m, and |R_P(A_S)−R_P(A_{S\setminus i})|≤β_m for every sample and index. All three conclusions are choice-free.

For the stated real RKHS with K(x,x)≤κ², measurable nonnegative convex σ-Lipschitz loss, λ>0 and attained retained-set minima, regularized ERM with objective n⁻¹∑_{j∈J}c(f(x_j),y_j)+λ‖f‖² is permutation-invariant and has uniform deletion stability β_m=σ²κ²/(2λm). For fixed λ this envelope is nonincreasing; no uniform loss bound M is supplied.
